layer_reason: The defect is in the emitted device structure of the Triton kernel (address form forces per-lane scalarization and an in-kernel serial N*C loop); it must be fixed by changing the kernel's tiling, index form and grid mapping, not by an IR pass or by tuning launch parameters (the kernel is 1000x off the reference, so no config choice can recover it).
simulator_incremental_judgment: The simulator adds two facts not derivable from source syntax: (1) the real device actually selected BLOCK_Y=1, so every program handles a single output row and the N*C loop is the only source of per-program parallelism, and (2) each of the four load sites is bracketed by BAR/WAIT_FLAG on VECTOR/SCALAR, i.e. per-load synchronization, which is consistent with the per-lane scalar load lowering seen in bcmlir. It does NOT add a usable total-time or per-load ranking: its capture window is explicitly partial (72 us observed for a 255 ms kernel, 'application did not finish'), so I do not use it as a quantitative claim and do not infer the mechanism from simulator presence alone.
